lines.text: The gold price waved tiny flags.
In 1919, five London firms met to fix the price of gold.
lines.say: In nineteen nineteen, five London firms met to fix the price of gold.

lines.text: They sat in a small panelled room at Rothschild's bank.
Each desk had a telephone and a small Union Jack flag.
Raising your flag meant not ready, and dealing stopped.
The chairman tried prices until buyers and sellers balanced.
The fixing paused in 1939 and came back in 1954.

post.caption: The gold price waved tiny flags. In 1919, five London firms met to fix the price of gold. They sat in a small panelled room at Rothschild's bank. Each desk had a telephone and a small Union Jack flag. Raising your flag meant not ready, and dealing stopped. The chairman tried prices until buyers and sellers balanced. The fixing paused in 1939 and came back in 1954. From 1968, the fix ran twice a day, in dollars. In 2004, Rothschild left, and the flags went out of use. The last London gold fix came in March 2015.
